processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching; this sample corresponds to 525 °C for 10 h.

structures.overall_structure: α (BCC) matrix with a small amount of β-Mn precipitated along the α grain boundaries and within the α grains, plus some small α-Mn particles in the α matrix; the α matrix has only partially transformed to β-Mn after aging at 525 °C for 10 h.

microstructure_list.region: bulk (α grain boundaries and α grain interiors)

phases_present.morphology: small amount precipitated along the α grain boundaries and within the α grains
small particles in the α matrix

precipitates.distribution: along the α grain boundaries and within the α grains
small particles dispersed in the α matrix

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure hardness of the 17Al alloy after the different aging treatments including 525 °C / 10 h.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 17Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 10 h reached 616.8 ± 12.3 HV (Table 3); at 525 °C hardness rose monotonically from 566.9 ± 9.7 HV (1 h) to 616.8 ± 12.3 HV (10 h).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification observations; samples electrolytically polished in 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases and β-Mn/α-Mn precipitation in the 17Al alloy after aging treatments, including 525 °C / 10 h.
characterization_methods.key_findings: After aging the 17Al alloy at 525 °C for 10 h, the phase map was dominated by BCC α with a green β-Mn network decorating the α grain boundaries and minor α-Mn particles; only 20.5 % β-Mn had formed.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Samples electrolytically polished in 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) in aged samples and the progress of the α → β-Mn transformation.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 17Al alloy, Fig. 8 shows that at 525 °C precipitation is sparse — rare β-Mn along α grain boundaries up to 6 h and only faint contrast of the α matrix at 10 h.

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the chemical composition of the alloys and of individual phases.
characterization_methods.key_findings: EDS-measured composition of the 17Al alloy is Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 (at.%) (Table 1).

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys after different aging treatments.
characterization_methods.key_findings: XRD patterns (Fig. 10) show α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn diffraction peaks in the selected aged samples, indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitate before the α matrix fully transforms to β-Mn.

unmapped_findings: For the 17Al alloy, aging at 525 °C for 10 h gave the lowest-hardness aged condition of its series (616.8 ± 12.3 HV), consistent with the slow β-Mn precipitation kinetics at this low aging temperature; only 20.5 % β-Mn had formed with the α matrix largely untransformed (b0041, b0030, b0038).

The increase in Al content slowed the β-Mn precipitation kinetics during aging: whereas the 15Al α matrix almost completely transformed to β-Mn within 3 h at 525 °C, the 17Al and 19Al alloys required 6 h and 10 h, respectively, at 550 °C, so the 525 °C/10 h condition for 17Al remained only partially transformed (b0065, b0053).
